methodologyMarkdown:
## Overview
The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea publishes its judgments, advisory opinions and orders. The case index at https://www.itlos.org/en/main/cases/list-of-cases/ is server-rendered HTML (traditional hierarchical URLs, not hash routes) and lists all ~36 cases.

## Search
No search API or verified search-URL template. Discovery is by browsing the list of cases.

## Filters
None exposed as URL parameters. The case number is embedded in slugs like /case-no-25/.

## Download
The list page links to per-case pages using the pattern /en/main/cases/list-of-cases/{case-slug}/ (e.g. .../case-no-1/ for the M/V SAIGA case). The actual judgment/order PDFs are published on each individual case page under the 'Reports of Judgments, Advisory Opinions and Orders', so download is a record-page (two-hop) flow: list -> case page -> PDF link. includeAllLinks is used to reach the case pages, then PDFs are extracted per case.

## Metadata & Enrichment
No item/DSpace API. Metadata (case number, parties) parsed from link text and slug. Enrichment mode is none.

## Limitations
Server-rendered, no headless browser required. But PDFs are not on the index; a crawler must visit each case page to obtain document links, so harvesting is two-hop.
probeNotes: WebFetch of https://www.itlos.org/en/main/cases/list-of-cases/ confirmed server-rendered HTML listing 36 cases with real links following /en/main/cases/list-of-cases/{slug}/ and /case-no-{N}/. Judgment PDFs are not on the list page (must be fetched per case). No API mentioned.
